inn_landlord.text: Welcome aboard, bor. The Broads have about a hundred and twenty-five miles of waterway you can boat on, and not one lock. Folk come from all over to drift about and bump into each other.
The wherries used to carry everything here: coal, grain, reed, beer. Big black sails, one man and a boy. There's still one or two sailing, old ones like the Albion, built in 1898.

inn_oldboy.text: You heard of Black Shuck? Great black dog with one eye, big as a calf. In 1577 he ran through the churches at Bungay and Blythburgh in a thunderstorm, and folk died. You can still see the scorch marks on Blythburgh door.
Shuck's been off up north lately, they say. Whitby. Liked the steps. We miss him, in a funny sort of way. You're not meant to miss a hellhound. We're Norfolk. We miss everything.
